# Intuit App Partner Program FAQ

Last updated: 2026-10-29

 General program

**What is the Intuit App Partner Program?**

The Intuit App Partner Program is a transformative update to our platform, designed to accommodate partners of all sizes with different levels of engagement. It provides four distinct partner tiers, with a set of benefits tailored to different levels of engagement. The program features an improved developer experience, access to premium APIs, go-to-market support, and the implementation of platform service fees.*

* *Geographical availability of the Intuit App Partner Program varies, and different rates may apply. Feature availability varies by tier, with some benefits requiring onboarding that may delay activation. Additional terms, fees, eligibility requirements, and conditions apply.*

**When did the Intuit App Partner Program officially launch?**

The program launched in the US on July 28, 2025. On November 3, 2025 we expanded the Intuit App Partner Program to our partners in the United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada (excluding Quebec).

**Are all apps automatically part of the Intuit App Partner Program? Can I opt out?**

All apps are automatically enrolled in the Intuit App Partner Program at the Builder tier. Currently, there’s no method to opt out, but the Builder tier is an uncharged tier. However, the Builder tier is subject to a capped limit of CorePlus API calls.

**My team has a strategic integration with Intuit. Will my app be subject to platform fees as part of the Intuit App Partner Program?**

Contact your Partner Development Manager at Intuit to determine whether your app will be subject to platform service fees under the Intuit App Partner Program.

**What’s the difference between the QuickBooks Solution Provider program and the Intuit App Partner Program?**

The Intuit App Partner Program and the Intuit QuickBooks Solution Provider (QSP) program are two separate programs that provide unique benefits and features. If you are both an Intuit QuickBooks Solution Provider and an Intuit App Developer, contact your QSP representative at Intuit to learn how these programs compare.

 Tiers and benefits

**Where can I find an overview of the partner tiers?**

The program includes four tiers: Builder, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Each tier offers a unique set of benefits designed to provide the resources, support, and growth opportunities needed to thrive in our ecosystem. For the full list of benefits and features, see the, see the [Intuit App Partner Program Guide](https://static.developer.intuit.com/resources/Intuit_App_Partner_Program_Guide.pdf).

**What happens if I’m currently listed on the Intuit App Marketplace but am not a Silver, Gold, or Platinum partner?**

If you’re currently listed on the Intuit App Marketplace but you are a Builder partner, your app listing will temporarily remain in place, but is subject to removal from the Intuit App Marketplace. To avoid a delisting, you must subscribe to Silver.

* *Marketplace listing is available to Gold and Platinum partners, but it is not a requirement for tier eligibility.*

**How do I know what partner tier my app is in? What determines this?**

Your partner tier will be displayed on the Intuit Developer Portal. As long as you meet the tier requirements, you are eligible to subscribe to that tier. The table below outlines the partner tier requirements, followed by a list of referenced terms and definitions.

![../../../_images/iapp_tier_criteria_2.png](https://static.developer.intuit.com/images/iapp_tier_criteria_2.png)

- **Compliance:** You must complete an Intuit-approved app assessment questionnaire, accept our updated Intuit Developer Terms of Service, and comply with the Intuit App Partner Program.
- **Payment method:** You must provide and maintain a valid payment method. We offer credit card, ACH, Pre-authorized Debit (PAD), and Direct Debit as available payment methods. See the table below for payment methods provided in each region.
- **Active connections:** Defined as individual Intuit QuickBooks Online or Intuit Enterprise Suite companies that have an active subscription and a valid, non-expired OAuth token.
**Are the partner tiers determined at the app level or at the workspace level?**

The partner tiers are determined at the workspace level. If you have multiple production apps under one workspace, the connections will be aggregated and used to determine tier qualification.

**How do I qualify for the next partner tier and what timeframe is used for qualification?**

If you meet the eligibility requirements of a higher tier, you can request an upgrade to that tier at any time. However, Program Eligibility Checkpoints occur twice per year. For details on this process, see the [Intuit App Partner Program Guide](https://static.developer.intuit.com/resources/Intuit_App_Partner_Program_Guide.pdf).

**Do I automatically get upgraded to the next tier if I meet the tier requirements?**

Partners in the Builder tier can choose to subscribe to the Silver tier and be automatically upgraded upon providing a valid payment method. Upgrades to the Gold and Platinum tiers are not automatic and require review.

**How do I upgrade to the next tier?**

The Intuit Developer Portal features a subscription management interface where you can upgrade to Silver directly or request an upgrade to Gold or Platinum.

**Can I cancel my subscription?**

Yes. You can cancel your subscription from within the Intuit Developer Portal at any time. If you cancel your subscription, you can continue to use your tier’s benefits until your next Billing Cycle, at which point you will be placed into the Builder tier.

**When will the benefits for my partner tier be available to me?**

Some benefits will be available starting from your Billing Cycle date. A Billing Cycle will be defined from the day you subscribe to a paid Tier. Other additional benefit features availability varies by tier, with some benefits requiring onboarding that may delay activation.

**Can I get access to higher throttling limits and API performance?**

Currently, access to higher throttling limits and enhanced API performance is not available.

**Can I get access to dedicated technical support?**

For detailed information about the benefits, including technical support, available at each tier level, see the [Intuit App Partner Program Guide](https://static.developer.intuit.com/resources/Intuit_App_Partner_Program_Guide.pdf).

**How will Intuit help my business grow?**

Partners in the Silver, Gold, and Platinum tiers will be eligible for go-to-market benefits, which increase with each partner tier. For details, see the [Intuit App Partner Program Guide](https://static.developer.intuit.com/resources/Intuit_App_Partner_Program_Guide.pdf).

 Premium APIs

**Are there premium APIs released as part of the Intuit App Partner Program?**

The App Partner Program includes access to several useful premium APIs, providing you with richer functionality and deeper integration with Intuit QuickBooks Online and Intuit Enterprise Suite: Projects API, Custom Fields API, Sales Tax API, Intuit QuickBooks Workforce API, and Dimensions API.

**Where do I find out more about the premium APIs?**

Links to detailed tutorials and API references are provided below:

- **Projects API:** Create [projects](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/manage-projects/set-create-projects-quickbooks-online/L9GAdLMyT_US_en_US?uid=mah6uk5b) and track their profitability. See [Get Started with the Project API](/app/developer/qbo/docs/workflows/manage-projects/get-started).
- **Custom Fields API:** Create up to 12 [custom fields](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/purchase-orders/create-edit-custom-fields-quickbooks-online/L56PQNif3_US_en_US?uid=lt7m5ihf) that can be used across an array of different transactions. See [Get started with the Custom Fields API](/app/developer/qbo/docs/workflows/create-custom-fields/get-started).
- **Sales Tax API:** Access the [automated sales tax](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/sales-taxes/set-use-automated-sales-tax-quickbooks-online/L4Lx8eL7V_US_en_US?uid=mah6vfac) feature to automatically calculate the correct sales tax for invoices and other transactions. See [Get started with the Sales Tax API](/app/developer/qbo/docs/workflows/calculate-sales-tax/get-started-sales-tax).
- **Intuit QuickBooks Workforce API:** Access multiple [pay types](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-ca/help-article/salaries-wages/understand-supported-pay-types-deductions-online/L9bwnybee_CA_en_CA?uid=ltowcvs2) such as salary, hourly, overtime, holiday, and more for enhanced Time Tracking. Available to Silver, Gold, and Platinum partners. See [Get Started with the Intuit QuickBooks Workforce API](/app/developer/payroll-time/docs/get-started).
- **Dimensions API:** Create and manage [dimensions](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/class-list/create-user-defined-classes/L3rVkxIuy_US_en_US?uid=md3c2e74) to track aspects of accounting data such as department, product line, site, and location in Intuit Enterprise Suite. See [Get started with the Dimensions API](/app/developer/ies/docs/workflows/manage-dimensions).
**Where can we access updated Postman collections or SDKs for the premium APIs?**

API documentation, sample code, and Postman collections for the premium APIs are available [here](/app/developer/qbo/docs/workflows).

 Fees

**What types of fees will my app be subject to?**

As part of the Intuit App Partner Program, platform service fees apply to those developers who receive benefits from participating in our Intuit Developer Platform. The Platform Service Fees consist of two components: a flat monthly program fee and a variable API fee.

- The monthly program fee differs per partner tier and unlocks specific benefits, CorePlus API credits, and an API rate card based on the tier. Only the Builder tier is not charged and is excluded from the Platform Service Fees. Refer to this [table](https://developer.intuit.com/partners/benefits) for the program fees, CorePlus API credits, and API rate card by tier for each region.
- The variable API fee differs by partner tier and is charged for usage of certain APIs above the CorePlus API credits available to that tier.
**How do I know if I will be subject to a fee?**

If you are a partner in the Builder tier, you won’t be subject to any Platform Service Fees and the Builder tier will be limited to 500,000 CorePlus API credits per month. Any CorePlus API calls made above the included monthly credit will be blocked entirely. If you are a partner in the Silver, Gold, or Platinum tiers, you will be subject to the flat monthly program fees associated with each tier and variable CorePlus API fees, as applicable. See the pricing model for further details.

**Where can I find the pricing model?**

Refer to [this article](https://help.developer.intuit.com/s/article/platform-service-fees) to review the pricing model that includes the flat program fees, API credits, and variable API fees for each tier.

**The pricing table mentions Core and CorePlus APIs. What does that mean?**

The combination of the endpoint called and HTTP method used determines whether an API call is classified as Core or CorePlus.

- **Core API calls** cover most data-in operations such as creating or updating invoices, bills, customers, vendors, etc. Core API calls are unmetered and uncharged.
- **CorePlus API calls** over most data-out operations such as reading accounts, querying company information, and fetching reports. CorePlus API calls are metered and charges may apply.
To see a full breakdown of API calls and their respective categories, [see this article](https://help.developer.intuit.com/s/article/API-classification-for-the-Intuit-App-Partner-Program).

**What’s the maximum number of API calls that can be made while remaining at the uncharged partner tier?**

By default, all partners will begin in the Builder tier and be afforded 500,000 CorePlus API calls per month without incurring any charges. Any subsequent calls made above this allotment will be blocked. To make additional API calls beyond this allotment, partners can upgrade to the Silver tier by providing a valid payment method in their account on the Intuit Developer Portal within your Workspace.

**What happens when I exceed the number of API calls for my current partner tier?**

Only the Builder tier has restrictions on the number of CorePlus API calls. If you exceed the allowed number of CorePlus API call credits in the Builder tier, you will begin to experience API errors. To make additional CorePlus API calls beyond the Builder tier API cap*, you can upgrade to the Silver tier by providing a valid payment method on the Intuit Developer Portal within your Workspace.

Partners in the Silver, Gold, or Platinum tier have no restriction on the number of CorePlus API calls. However, charges will be incurred for any CorePlus API calls above the tier-specific API credits. Refer to the following table [here](https://developer.intuit.com/partners/benefits#:~:text=Variable%20API%20fees%20(Price%20per%201%20thousand%20CorePlus%20API%20calls) to reference monthly program fees, API credits, and API rate card by tier for each region.

* *Capped upper limit of 500,000 CorePlus API calls per calendar month.*

You can review some examples of our model based on different tiers and usage patterns in [this article](https://help.developer.intuit.com/s/article/platform-service-fees).

**Is API usage metered at the app or workspace level?**

API usage is metered at the app level and aggregated at the workspace level. If you have multiple production apps within one workspace, all usage will be aggregated and weighed against the pricing table and to determine your eligibility for a specific tier.

**Are there APIs where API credits and platform service fees do not apply?**

Yes. The following APIs will not be metered and will not be subject to variable API fees:

- [Payments API](/app/developer/qbpayments/docs/api/resources/all-entities/bankaccounts)
- [Desktop API](/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference)
- [Intuit QuickBooks Workforce API](/app/developer/gql/docs/api/qbexternal/queries/payrollEmployerInfo)
- [All OAuth endpoints](https://developer.api.intuit.com/.well-known/openid_configuration) - discovery document, access token, refresh, revoke, userinfo, JWKS
- All sandbox endpoints
Developers on the Intuit Developer Platform who use these APIs are still subject to the monthly program fee.

**My app is not published on the Intuit App Marketplace. Do the platform service fees apply to me?**

Yes. The platform service fees apply to all partners with production apps, whether or not your app is published on the Intuit App Marketplace.

**Is an Intuit App Marketplace listing required to qualify for Gold or Platinum tier?**

No. An Intuit App Marketplace listing is no longer a requirement for Gold or Platinum tier eligibility. While a listing is available to Gold and Platinum partners and unlocks additional marketing benefits (such as app badging, the feature rotator, and referral management), it is entirely optional. Your tier eligibility is determined by your number of active connections and compliance with program requirements.

**I was asked to create an app on your platform because I need credentials to be used on another platform or with a systems integrator. Do the platform service fees apply to me?**

Yes. Platform service fees apply to all partners with production apps in Silver, Gold, or Platinum workspaces.

 Usage and metrics

**When did Intuit start to track API usage?**

CorePlus API metering began November 3, 2025, for partners in the US, Canada (excluding Quebec), UK, and Australia. Variable API fees apply if usage exceeds the CorePlus API credit amount included with the monthly program fee for your selected partner tier. For partners choosing to stay in the Builder tier, there is a maximum monthly CorePlus API call limit of 500,000.

**How does Intuit determine where I am located?**

All developers are required to provide a company address associated with each Intuit Developer Portal workspace as part of your account creation.

**Where can I find metrics on my API usage?**

An API usage chart is available on the Intuit Developer Portal, providing you with insights into your API usage patterns. Under each app, you can navigate to the **Analytics** tab to view API calls by category (Core and CorePlus).

**Are calls to the sandbox API also metered and charged?**

No. Only production API calls are metered and charged.

**Are API calls to the QuickBooks Online free trial account metered and charged?**

Yes. All production API calls will be metered regardless of the subscription status of the QuickBooks Online company.

**Are calls that error out also metered and charged?**

No. Intuit only meters and charges successful API calls in production.

**Who can see the API usage chart?**

Users with *owner* or *admin* roles in your Intuit Team are able to view the API usage chart for your app.

**What if my API usage changes month to month?**

You will be charged according to your usage. If one month your usage is under the included API credits, then you will not incur a variable API fee. If the next month, your usage is over the included credits based on your tier, then you will incur variable API fees.

**When can I expect CorePlus API calls to stop failing once I subscribe to Silver Tier?**

When you subscribe to Silver Tier, the default Builder Tier 500,000 cap on CorePlus API calls will be lifted within one hour from the time you successfully enter a payment method and subscribe.

**What period does the CorePlus usage limit cover?**

The 500,000 CorePlus API call limit for the Builder Tier works on a monthly basis. This call limit resets on the 1st of each new month. Note that the limit cannot be reset at any other point in time.

 Billing

**What are the Developer Platform Service Fees?**

The Intuit Developer Platform Service Fees include a flat monthly program fee (“Program Fee”) and a variable API Fee (“API Fee”) based upon the subscribed tier and the actual API usage, plus any applicable fees and taxes. Refer to the table [here](https://developer.intuit.com/partners/benefits#:~:text=Variable%20API%20fees%20(Price%20per%201%20thousand%20CorePlus%20API%20calls)) for the program fee, API credits, and API rate card by tier for each region.

**What is the billing cycle for the Developer Platform Service Fees?**

A Billing Cycle date is defined from the date you enter a payment method and subscribe to a paid tier. Flat Program Fees are charged monthly in advance while variable API Fees are charged at the end of the Billing Cycle, as applicable. During each Billing Cycle, an invoice will be created that details the flat monthly Program Fee along with any variable API Fees, if applicable. Payment for these fees will be processed on the same day the invoice is created.

**How are Program Fees assessed and charged?**

Flat Program Fees are assessed in advance each month, charged on your designated Billing Cycle date and prorated based on your designated Billing Cycle date.

**How are variable API fees assessed and charged?**

Variable API fees are assessed in arrears and charged on your next billing date. These fees account for any usage exceeding the CorePlus API credit limit during the previous Billing Cycle.

**Can you provide an example (in USD) billing scenario for the variable API fee?**

*November 10, 2025*

- A partner subscribes to the Silver tier.
- The first monthly Program Fee is charged for $300 USD, covering the period of November 10, 2025 - December 10, 2025.
*November 10, 2025 - December 10, 2025*

- This partner successfully initiated 1.5 million CorePlus API calls in this period.
*December 10, 2025*

- A $300 USD monthly Program Fee is charged.
- A variable API fee is assessed covering the period of November 10, 2025 - December 10, 2025.
- The variable API Fee is incurred for any CorePlus API calls in excess of the included CorePlus API credits in USD:
  - 1,000,000 calls at $0/1000 (included CorePlus API credits in Silver Tier).
  - 500,000 calls at $3.50/1000 (exceeds the CorePlus API credits in Silver Tier).
**Can you provide an example (in UK) billing scenario for the variable API fee?**

*November 10 2025*

- A partner subscribes to the Silver tier.
- The first monthly Program Fee is charged for £225.
- This partner successfully initiated 1.5 million CorePlus API calls in this period.
- The variable API Fee is incurred for any CorePlus API calls in excess of the included CorePlus API credits:
  - 1,000,000 calls at £0/1000 (included CorePlus API credits in Silver Tier).
  - 500,000 calls at £2.60/1000 (exceeds the CorePlus API credits in Silver Tier).
**Can you provide an example (in Canada, excluding Quebec) billing scenario for the variable API fee?**

*November 10 2025*

- A partner subscribes to the Silver tier.
- The first monthly Program Fee is charged for $425.
- This partner successfully initiated 1.5 million CorePlus API calls in this period.
- The variable API Fee is incurred for any CorePlus API calls in excess of the included CorePlus API credits:
  - 1,000,000 calls at $0/1000 (included CorePlus API credits in Silver Tier).
  - 500,000 calls at $4.85/1000 (exceeds the CorePlus API credits in Silver Tier).
**Why am I seeing a $0 entry on my payment method’s transaction history?**

During the downgrade process, a temporary $0 authorization may appear in your transaction history. This entry is not permanent and is used to verify the payment method.

 Payment

**What payment methods are accepted for paying the API fees?**

**Payment Methods:**

![../../../_images/iapp_pricing_model_2.png](https://static.developer.intuit.com/images/iapp_pricing_model_2.png)
**What payment terms are offered by Intuit to pay the bill?**

Payment is automatically collected the same day the invoice is provided.

**Do I need to provide my credit card information if I’m operating at the Builder tier?**

No. You don’t need to provide a payment method if you are at the Builder tier. However, if you make more than 500,000 CorePlus API calls in a one-month time period, you will need to provide a payment method to upgrade to the Silver tier in order to continue calling APIs at the same rate and to avoid service and throttling issues.

**What happens if my payment method does not work when Intuit sends me a bill for my API usage (e.g., if my credit card has expired)?**

In the case of payment failure, Intuit provides a grace period at our discretion in order for you to update your payment method or provide a new payment method. Providing a valid payment method will automatically retry the charge. If the charge is still in collections after the grace period, all API calls for apps in your workspace will be blocked.

**What happens if I do not provide a payment method?**

Partners who do not provide a payment method will be placed in the Builder tier, which includes access to 500,000 CorePlus API calls per month.

**When will I receive my first bill?**

The first flat program fee will be assessed on the day you provide a valid payment method and prorated based on your Billing Cycle, which starts from the date you provide a payment method.

**If I’m a developer with multiple apps, will I get a separate bill for each app?**

A bill is sent for each workspace. If a partner has three total apps and they all reside in one workspace, that partner will receive one bill with the usage aggregated across all three apps. However, if you have three workspaces with an app in each workspace, then you will receive three separate invoices, one for each workspace.

**If I need additional time for making payments, will I incur late fees?**

In the case of payment failure, Intuit will provide a grace period at our discretion in order for you to provide a new or updated payment method; however, there are no late fees. Providing a valid payment method will automatically retry the charge. If the charge is still in collections after the grace period, all API calls for apps in your workspace will be blocked.

**What’s the process to request late payment?**

Currently, there’s no process to request a late payment.

**Does Intuit provide best practices for reducing CorePlus calls?**

We have created the following blog posts to help you understand some best practices for reducing CorePlus calls.

- [Best Practices for Intuit API Optimization: Part 1](https://blogs.intuit.com/2025/08/11/best-practices-for-intuit-api-optimization-part-1/)
- [Best Practices for Intuit API Optimization: Part 2](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://blogs.intuit.com/2025/10/24/best-practices-for-intuit-api-optimization-part-2/&sa=D&source=docs&ust=1769118489416344&usg=AOvVaw1xRTIeLGj0WRlV07wypsXP)
**Are there plans to introduce enterprise tiers beyond Platinum or adjust credit allocations annually?**

Currently, this isn’t in the plan. However, we are keen to hear feedback about the program and make updates in the future. We will share this feedback with the team so we can consider introducing it in the future.

 Net Terms

**What are Net Terms and who is eligible?**

Net Terms allows eligible Intuit App Partner Program (IAPP) Platinum partners to pay their monthly invoices within 30 days of invoice issuance instead of making an immediate payment at billing.

Current eligibility requirements:

- Must be an IAPP Platinum partner
- Must be a US-based partner (determined by the company address in your workspace)
- Must successfully complete a credit assessment
**Where can I apply for Net Terms and is a credit check required?**

You can apply directly through the Intuit Developer Portal by navigating to the **Billing & subscription** tab, clicking the pencil icon to edit your payment method, and selecting the Net Terms option.

As part of the process, a credit assessment is required to determine eligibility.

The process is fully digital and does not require a sales call or physical documentation.

Please note that submitting your application, you authorize Intuit to share your business information with a third-party provider to conduct a credit assessment. This assessment may include a review of your business credit profile. You will be notified of the outcome.

**How can I apply for Net Terms in the Developer Portal?**

1. Log in to your Intuit Developer Portal account
2. Choose a relevant workspace
3. Navigate to **Billing & subscription** tab
4. You’ll see your current payment method and billing information
5. Click the pencil icon next to your current payment method
6. Select “Net Terms” as your payment option (alongside the current Immediate payment option)
7. Click “Apply for Net Terms” to start the application
8. Complete the application
9. Submit — a credit assessment runs automatically
10. Wait for decision — your application status will show as Pending until reviewed
11. Once your Net Terms application is processed and approved, log in and toggle to the net terms ‘Invoice 30’ option under the pencil icon
12. Your account will be updated accordingly and your next invoice will automatically reflect the Net 30 payment terms.
**How will I know if I’m approved and when do Net Terms become active?**

You will receive a notification via email regarding your application status after the credit assessment is completed.

If approved, you must review, accept, and activate Net Terms in your payment profile. Once activated, Net Terms will automatically apply to your next invoice and all future invoices unless you or Intuit modify your payment settings in accordance with the applicable terms.

**What happens If my Net Terms application is rejected ?**

If your Net Terms application is rejected, you will remain on your current immediate payment terms.

**What payment methods are supported under Net Terms?**

Approved partners can pay invoices using:

- Credit Card (CC)
- ACH
- Wire Transfer
Wire transfer instructions and Intuit banking details will be included with invoices.

**Where can I view my invoices and billing history?**

You can view invoice details and payment status, including paid and partially paid invoices, directly from your Developer Portal account within the **Billing and Subscription** tab.

**Do I need to reapply for future invoices?**

No. Once Net Terms are activated, they automatically apply to all eligible future invoices unless you or Intuit update the payment settings.

**Can I switch back to immediate payment terms?**

Yes. You may request to return to immediate payment terms at any time, provided there are no outstanding Net Terms invoices on your account.

**Can Intuit change or revoke Net Terms eligibility?**

Yes. Net Terms are subject to credit approval, ongoing eligibility requirements, and program policies, which may change over time.

**When can I apply for Net Terms?**

You can apply for Net Terms beginning May 28, 2026, through your payment profile in the Intuit Developer Portal. Applications are available on an ongoing basis to eligible Platinum partners.

**Do I need to contact PDM or complete paperwork?**

No. The process is fully self-serve and does not require PDM engagement or manual paperwork.

**What happens if I have unpaid Net Terms invoices?**

Outstanding invoices may impact your program eligibility and affect future eligibility for Net Terms. Partners shall remain obligated to pay all outstanding invoices in accordance with the applicable agreement.

**What happens when payments are overdue?**

Automated payment reminders will be sent and your account will be flagged, If payment is not received by the invoice due date,access to certain Intuit App Partner Program benefits, features, may be temporarily paused until the balance is paid. Partners can restore good standing by settling the outstanding balance. Repeated delinquency may affect future eligibility for net terms billing.

**How long will it take to process a Net Terms application to get approved?**

Processing times may vary. You will be notified via email once a decision is reached.Once submitted, your Net Terms application will be reviewed by our credit assessment team. We will notify you of the outcome via email once the review is complete.

 Resources

**How do I access the Partner Resource Center?**

As part of the program*, you’ll gain access to the Intuit Partner Resource Center (PRC) to assist with your QuickBooks marketing initiatives. Access to specific features and benefits is determined by your partner tier. PRC access is now fully automated and updates in near real-time. Whether you subscribe, upgrade, downgrade, or cancel, your permissions are adjusted automatically without the need for support tickets. Partners in the Silver, Gold, and Platinum tiers can seamlessly access enablement content, playbooks, and co-marketing assets specific to their level.

* *Eligibility and access are subject to program terms and tier requirements.*

Your PRC account is private and unique to your company, with access controlled by you. To set up your license quickly, please look for a Welcome email from `no-reply@partnerprogram.intuit.com` in your inbox.

If you didn’t receive this Welcome email:

1. Check your junk/spam folder.
2. If you can’t locate it, click on the **Forgot Your Password** link on the [PRC sign-in page](https://intuit.ziftone.com/#/page/isv-dev-home-v2).
3. You can also send an email to contact `support@ziftone.com` for help.
Once you’ve gained access, head over to the [Marketing Onboarding page](https://intuit.ziftone.com/#/page/login) to discover how the PRC can help power your growth with QuickBooks!

 Support

**Who can I contact if I have more questions?**

You can contact our developer support team by submitting a [ticket](https://help.developer.intuit.com/s/contactsupport). When you create a ticket regarding the Intuit App Partner Program, select the product **Intuit App Partner Program** and the appropriate category for faster routing.

You can visit the Intuit Developer Support [website](https://help.developer.intuit.com/s/) and select one of our forums to post a question. You can also scroll to the Webinars and Office Hours section to review a list of upcoming webinars and office hours, along with links to sign up for each event.
